# Fix: 1px White Line at Top of Video Thumbnails on Hover

## Context

When hovering over project thumbnails in the video gallery, a 1px white line appears at the top of each video. This happens when the Vimeo iframe fades in over the static thumbnail. The white line is from the Vimeo player's internal rendering — Vimeo's `background: true` mode injects an iframe whose content has a thin white artifact at the top edge (likely an internal UI element or anti-aliasing seam).

The site background is `#141414`, so even 1px of white is very noticeable.

## Root Cause

In `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx`, the video layer container (lines 326-341) has `overflow: hidden` and `borderRadius: 6px`, but the Vimeo iframe sits flush against the top edge (`top-0`). The white pixel is the Vimeo player's own top-edge artifact bleeding through.

## Approach: Clip the Top Edge with `inset`

Use CSS `inset` to pull the iframe container down by 1px at the top, effectively cropping away the white artifact. The parent already has `overflow: hidden`, so this clips cleanly.

This is better than alternatives like:
- Negative margin (shifts layout)
- CSS `clip-path` (extra rendering layer)
- `top: -1px` with increased height (fragile)

## Changes

### 1. `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx` (line 337-340)

Change the inner container ref div from `inset-0` to explicit inset values that crop 1px off the top:

```tsx
// Before:
<div
  ref={containerRef}
  className="absolute inset-0 w-full h-full"
/>

// After:
<div
  ref={containerRef}
  className="absolute w-full h-full"
  style={{ top: '-1px', left: 0, right: 0, bottom: 0 }}
/>
```

By setting `top: -1px`, the iframe content shifts up 1px inside the `overflow: hidden` parent, cropping the white artifact off the top. The bottom extends 1px below but is also clipped by the parent's overflow.

### 2. `app/globals.css` — Belt-and-suspenders iframe rule

Add `border: none` and `display: block` to the existing Vimeo iframe rule. Some browsers add a default 1-2px border on iframes, and `display: inline` can cause sub-pixel gaps:

```css
/* Before: */
iframe[src*="vimeo"],
iframe[src*="player.vimeo"] {
  background-color: #141414;
}

/* After: */
iframe[src*="vimeo"],
iframe[src*="player.vimeo"] {
  background-color: #141414;
  border: none;
  display: block;
}
```

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx` | Shift inner container 1px up to crop Vimeo's top-edge artifact |
| `app/globals.css` | Add `border: none; display: block` to Vimeo iframe rule |

## Also Pending (from earlier in this session)

The previous card spacing + font size changes are already staged but uncommitted:
- `components/ChatProjectCard.tsx` — increased card margins (20px top, 12px bottom)
- `components/ChatBot.tsx` — bot reply font 17px -> 16.5px

These will be committed alongside the thumbnail fix.

## Verification

1. `npx next build` — confirm clean build
2. Open site, hover over gallery thumbnails
3. Confirm no white pixel line at the top of any video
4. Confirm video still plays smoothly on hover and stops on leave
5. Check that border-radius corners still look clean (no sharp edges)
6. Test the one cinematic-ratio project to ensure the `2.39:1` aspect ratio still works

# Fix: White Pixel Artifacts on ALL Edges of Video Thumbnails

## Context

The previous fix (shifting `top: -1px`) eliminated the white line at the top but now white pixels are visible on the **left and right edges**. The Vimeo iframe's `background: true` mode produces a 1px white artifact on all four edges, not just the top. The parent div has `overflow: hidden` and `borderRadius: 6px`, so the fix is to make the iframe container bleed 1px past the parent on **every side**.

## Current State (after previous partial fix)

```tsx
// components/VideoThumbnail.tsx lines 337-340
<div
  ref={containerRef}
  className="absolute w-full h-full"
  style={{ top: '-1px', left: 0, right: 0, bottom: 0 }}
/>
```

This only crops the top edge. Left, right, and bottom are flush — white pixels still visible on sides.

## Fix

### 1. `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx` (line 337-340)

Use negative inset on all four sides. Remove `w-full h-full` since absolute positioning with all four inset values defines the size automatically.

```tsx
// After:
<div
  ref={containerRef}
  className="absolute"
  style={{ top: '-1px', left: '-1px', right: '-1px', bottom: '-1px' }}
/>
```

This makes the iframe 2px wider and 2px taller than its parent, centered. The parent's `overflow: hidden` clips all four edges, removing white artifacts everywhere. The `borderRadius: 6px` on the parent ensures corners remain rounded.

### 2. `app/globals.css` — No additional changes needed

The `border: none; display: block` rule added previously is still good belt-and-suspenders.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx` | Negative 1px inset on all four sides (was only top) |

## Verification

1. `npx next build` — clean build
2. Hover over gallery thumbnails — no white pixels on any edge (top, bottom, left, right)
3. Video still plays on hover and stops on leave
4. Border-radius corners still look clean
5. Cinematic `2.39:1` aspect ratio project still works correctly

# Fix: 1px White Line at Top of Video Thumbnails on Hover

## Context

When hovering over project thumbnails in the video gallery, a 1px white line appears at the top of each video. This happens when the Vimeo iframe fades in over the static thumbnail. The white line is from the Vimeo player's internal rendering — Vimeo's `background: true` mode injects an iframe whose content has a thin white artifact at the top edge (likely an internal UI element or anti-aliasing seam).

The site background is `#141414`, so even 1px of white is very noticeable.

## Root Cause

In `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx`, the video layer container (lines 326-341) has `overflow: hidden` and `borderRadius: 6px`, but the Vimeo iframe sits flush against the top edge (`top-0`). The white pixel is the Vimeo player's own top-edge artifact bleeding through.

## Approach: Clip the Top Edge with `inset`

Use CSS `inset` to pull the iframe container down by 1px at the top, effectively cropping away the white artifact. The parent already has `overflow: hidden`, so this clips cleanly.

This is better than alternatives like:
- Negative margin (shifts layout)
- CSS `clip-path` (extra rendering layer)
- `top: -1px` with increased height (fragile)

## Changes

### 1. `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx` (line 337-340)

Change the inner container ref div from `inset-0` to explicit inset values that crop 1px off the top:

```tsx
// Before:
<div
  ref={containerRef}
  className="absolute inset-0 w-full h-full"
/>

// After:
<div
  ref={containerRef}
  className="absolute w-full h-full"
  style={{ top: '-1px', left: 0, right: 0, bottom: 0 }}
/>
```

By setting `top: -1px`, the iframe content shifts up 1px inside the `overflow: hidden` parent, cropping the white artifact off the top. The bottom extends 1px below but is also clipped by the parent's overflow.

### 2. `app/globals.css` — Belt-and-suspenders iframe rule

Add `border: none` and `display: block` to the existing Vimeo iframe rule. Some browsers add a default 1-2px border on iframes, and `display: inline` can cause sub-pixel gaps:

```css
/* Before: */
iframe[src*="vimeo"],
iframe[src*="player.vimeo"] {
  background-color: #141414;
}

/* After: */
iframe[src*="vimeo"],
iframe[src*="player.vimeo"] {
  background-color: #141414;
  border: none;
  display: block;
}
```

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `components/VideoThumbnail.tsx` | Shift inner container 1px up to crop Vimeo's top-edge artifact |
| `app/globals.css` | Add `border: none; display: block` to Vimeo iframe rule |

## Also Pending (from earlier in this session)

The previous card spacing + font size changes are already staged but uncommitted:
- `components/ChatProjectCard.tsx` — increased card margins (20px top, 12px bottom)
- `components/ChatBot.tsx` — bot reply font 17px -> 16.5px

These will be committed alongside the thumbnail fix.

## Verification

1. `npx next build` — confirm clean build
2. Open site, hover over gallery thumbnails
3. Confirm no white pixel line at the top of any video
4. Confirm video still plays smoothly on hover and stops on leave
5. Check that border-radius corners still look clean (no sharp edges)
6. Test the one cinematic-ratio project to ensure the `2.39:1` aspect ratio still works
